original_test_intent: Perform exactly one approved BIOS upgrade or downgrade via the supported Redfish workflow and prove image acceptance, terminal task success, one expected BMC reset and full platform recovery at the intended version.
original_method: Bind target and signed BIOS image, preserve a full baseline, execute the vendor-defined UpdateService workflow under attended control, monitor task/reset/readiness, and compare post-flash firmware, inventory, logs and health.
manual_activity: The owner selects direction/image and approves the destructive maintenance window and recovery plan; an operator supervises stable power, console, task/reset timeline and any recovery while automation performs only the approved workflow.
required_inputs: Selected upgrade or downgrade and signed image digest
Stable power, independent console and rollback/recovery path
safety_requirements: Treat the flash as destructive and require explicit approval
Use only authenticated compatible image and documented Redfish path
Keep power stable and prohibit concurrent firmware operations
Do not clear logs before baseline
Count task-induced reset separately from extra reset or power loss
Never auto-retry or add an AC cycle
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, image, direction and compatibility
Preserve baseline and start task/reset/console monitoring
Execute only the approved Redfish transfer and monitor to terminal state
Verify one reset, BMC/OS readiness, BIOS version, inventory, logs and health
Do not choose image/direction, recover autonomously or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve image, direction, window and recovery
Supervise mutation and authorize any recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Completely inapplicable: CEMBB sensor reads belong to duplicate row 776 and cannot perform or verify BIOS flash.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-reviewed Redfish BIOS UpdateService client/schema with secret-safe transport and task monitoring only after all approval and recovery gates pass.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Upgrade/downgrade scope, Redfish method, single-reset criterion and 15/15-minute values are retained; exactly one direction is selected per execution.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run a baseline-task-reset-recovery state machine with immutable image identity and evidence at every transition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing package authenticity, compatibility, task semantics and recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; successful flash, intended version, one reset and recovered health all remain mandatory.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong image, power loss or failed activation can render the host unbootable and require recovery.

project_override_considerations: A project may choose upgrade or downgrade and the supported Redfish transfer mode, but must bind one authenticated image and document reset semantics, rollback and any deviation from the stated single-reset oracle.
expected_evidence: Approval, target identity, current/target versions and signed image digest
Redacted UpdateService request/response and task transitions
Exactly one BMC reset and availability timeline
Recovery record if invoked and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1498 consistently defines a Redfish BIOS flash; duplicate row 776 is isolated by variant and remains a CEMBB thermal case.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Image, vendor schema, approval, stable power and recovery controls are normal finite prerequisites. Execution is prohibited until supplied but is not permanently impossible.

review_improvement: Replaces unrelated sensor reads with a complete destructive-firmware state machine and an auditable one-reset and recovery oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: The action and success criteria are clear, but safe execution depends on exact target/image compatibility, vendor protocol and recovery ownership. Those finite prerequisites mandate REQUIRES; no generic command or validator result can authorize the flash.
